newsitem.title: UK: Portman building society 1996 net lending jumps.
newsitem.headline: Portman building society 1996 net lending jumps.

text.p: British regional mortgage lender and savings group the Portman Building Society, said on Wednesday that strong growth in its total retail receipts in 1996 had supported an improvement in its market share, though its net interest income and pretax profit fell in the year.
The society, which concentrates in the south of England, saw its net retail receipts rise 96 percent to 321 million stg and gross mortgage lending rise by 48 percent to 829 million stg.
In the meantime its net interest income dipped to 64.2 million stg from 68.6 million stg in 1995, while its pretax profit slipped 4.8 percent to 34.3 million stg.
In comments on the results, the society's chief executive Ken Culley said the results showed "an outstanding performance".
"The mortgage finance industry is approaching a crossroads with the impending conversion to listed plc status of four of the top six building societies," he added.
"Conversions and takeovers will leave the banks with by far the largest share of the retail savings and mortgage markets but building societies will nevertheless remain a dynamic industry.

"With its financial strength and distinctive position in the savings and mortgage markets, Portman will continue to... offer products and interest rates that our competitors will find difficult to match," Culley said.
